title_as_printed: Experimental dew points temperatures and pressures for binary mixtures {(1-y) propane + y water}
pressure_note: pressure of the dew point measurement (line pressure at the chilled-mirror instrument), pressure transmitter; total pressure of the binary mixture; unit 10^5 Pa as printed in header

value.what: y of the generated wet gas, printed in the block label row 'y = ...'; calculated by the authors from the Karl Fischer water content (10^-6 kg m^-3 (n)) times 10^-6*22.4/18.01; dew point T is the measured quantity at that y and P

conversion_needs: The dew curve is a function of y: each block is one isoplethic dew-point curve; builder should treat y_h2o at the printed (T,P) as the stated y (derived by authors)
notes: Side-by-side two-column printing (T,P left and right pairs) was stacked: left column of each block read downwards, then the right column; order within a block is therefore the printed order (monotonic increasing in T and P). Many points lie below 273.15 K: whether the condensed phase is liquid water or ice is not stated.
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: see Table 2 remark on very low water content
caution: Derived water mole fractions from Karl Fischer water content; at the lowest-water, low-pressure nitrogen points y*P/psat(T) is only 0.6-0.76, which is not physical; the authors attribute their largest deviations to error at very low water content.
